review_scope: Complete Chinese–English alignment reading with title and deck. Existing full prose retained; seven local corrections awaiting independent second review. Source historical claims are separate author questions, not silently changed in translation.

changes.before: Start with something that looks like common sense and is almost always lost once a war is actually underway.
changes.after: Start with something that looks like common sense and is very easy to lose once a war is actually underway.
changes.reason: 极容易 describes vulnerability, not an almost-always frequency claim.

changes.before: The preparation meant here is not military buildup; that belongs to soldiers. It has three layers.
changes.after: The preparation meant here is not military buildup; that is the work of military strategists. It has three layers.
changes.reason: 军事家 denotes the military specialists/decision-makers, not all soldiers.

changes.before: 5. Cultivation Without Suppression Has Another Name
changes.after: 5. Cultivation Without Suppression Is Called Development
changes.reason: Restore 发展 in the actual section heading, not only in the following paragraph.

changes.before: This is not a word swap. When subjectivity is released, cultivation grows on its own. When subjects recognize one another, it deepens on its own. When a civilization is not interrupted, it accumulates into visible results — science, art, technology, organization, thought, an entire flourishing. All of these are cultivation showing on the outside.
changes.after: This is not a word swap. When subjectivity is released, cultivation grows on its own. When subjects recognize one another, it deepens on its own. When a civilization is not interrupted, it accumulates into visible results — a flourishing of science, art, technology, organization, thought, and aesthetics. All of these are cultivation showing on the outside.
changes.reason: Restore the omitted aesthetics and the full scope of flourishing.

changes.before: A side that releases cultivation activates a feedback loop of creativity, judgment, and cooperation, and that loop produces a faster rate of development — because development just is cultivation accumulating uninterrupted. A side that suppresses cultivation cannot activate the loop: suppressed subjects either produce less out of withdrawal, or consume social resources through resistance, or lose the capacity for long-range planning under fear. The gap between the two rates compounds.
changes.after: A side that releases cultivation activates a positive feedback loop of creativity, judgment, and cooperation, and that loop produces a faster rate of development — because development just is cultivation accumulating uninterrupted. A side that suppresses cultivation cannot activate the loop: suppressed subjects either produce less out of withdrawal, or consume social resources through resistance, or lose the capacity for long-range planning under fear. The gap between the two rates accumulates exponentially over time.
changes.reason: Restore 正反馈 and the explicit exponent/time wording. This preserves the authorial assertion rather than independently proving it.

changes.after: It means a high probability of prevailing, not inevitable victory.
changes.reason: Make the object 胜出 explicit while preserving the probabilistic limitation.

changes.before: If a Kingdom of Ends depends on winning wars to survive, it is structurally disadvantaged — because it is not good at war. Its cultivation mechanisms have to be partly inhibited in wartime, or no unified action is possible at all. If it depends instead on the continued deepening of cultivation, it is structurally advantaged, because that is what it does every day anyway.
changes.after: If a Kingdom of Ends depends on winning wars to survive, it is structurally disadvantaged — because it is not good at war. Its cultivation mechanisms have to be partly inhibited in wartime, or no unified military action is possible. If it depends instead on the continued deepening of cultivation, it is structurally advantaged, because that is what it does every day anyway.
changes.reason: The source is unified war action, not the impossibility of every collective action.

unresolved_source_questions.finding: Assyrian imperial collapse is conflated with discontinuation of its civilization; scholarly post-imperial evidence contradicts disappearance without trace.
Spartan demographic decline is conflated with disappearance and denial of military defeat; Leuctra and later Hellenistic Sparta require qualifications.
Spain/Netherlands contrast compresses chronology, claims no Dutch natural resources, and overstates printing and Morisco geography; still gathering precise sources before proposing author amendments.

metadata_changes.before: A war completes outside itself. Real losing is breaking your own civilization's cultivation along the way — so a war can be won militarily and lost structurally. Not fighting is also preparing: deepening cultivation in peacetime is the best preparation there is.
metadata_changes.after: A war always completes outside itself. Real losing is breaking your own civilization's cultivation along the way — so a war can be won militarily and lost structurally. Not fighting is also preparing: deepening cultivation in peacetime is the best preparation there is.
metadata_changes.reason: Restore 永远 in the deck.
